sections.learningObjectives:
- Identify common medical prefixes (location, number, size, negation) and suffixes (condition, procedure, disease) and state their meanings.
- Explain how prefixes and suffixes modify the meaning of a word root or combining form.
- Build medical terms by combining roots with appropriate prefixes and suffixes.
- Decode unfamiliar medical terms by breaking them into prefix, root, and suffix components.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Sub- is like saying something is "under" the table. A subcutaneous injection goes under the skin, just like something hidden under a table.

### Question 2

Intra- means "inside." Think of an intravenous (IV) line as a tiny straw that goes inside a vein, not next to it.

### Question 3

Inter- means "between," like the space between two parked cars. The intercostal spaces are the gaps between your ribs.

### Question 4

Epi- means "on top," like icing on top of a cake. The epidermis is the top layer of your skin, sitting on top of the layer below it.

### Question 5

Hypo- means "too little," like a phone battery that is almost empty. An underactive thyroid is running low, just like that battery.

### Question 6

Hyper- means "too much," like a balloon blown up with too much air. High blood pressure is like too much push inside the blood vessels.

### Question 7

Endo- means "inside," like looking inside a closed box through a small window. An endoscope lets a provider look inside the body.

### Question 8

Retro- means "behind," like a car backing up. Retroperitoneal organs sit behind the lining inside your belly.

### Question 9

Para- can mean "next to," like a friend sitting beside you in class. The parathyroid glands sit right next to the thyroid.

### Question 10

Bi- means "two," like a bicycle with two wheels. "Bilateral" simply means both sides.

### Question 11

Hemi- means "half," like cutting a sandwich in half. Hemiplegia means one half of the body cannot move.

### Question 12

Poly- means "a lot," like a bag of many marbles. Polyuria means making a lot of urine.

### Question 13

Mono- means "one," like a unicycle with one wheel. A monocyte is named for having one big nucleus.

### Question 14

Quadri- means "four," like a square with four corners. Quadriplegia affects all four arms and legs.

### Question 15

Tri- means "three," like a tricycle with three wheels. The triceps muscle has three parts.

### Question 16

Oligo- means "just a little," like a trickle of water instead of a steady stream. Oliguria means making only a tiny amount of urine.

### Question 17

Primi- means "first," like being first in line. A primigravida is someone having her first pregnancy.

### Question 18

Micro- means "tiny," like an ant compared to an elephant. A microscope helps us see tiny things.

### Question 19

Macro- means "big," like an elephant compared to an ant. Something macroscopic is big enough to see without a microscope.

### Question 20

Megalo- and -megaly mean "grown too big," like a balloon blown up extra large. Hepatomegaly means the liver got too big.

### Question 21

Macrocytic means the cells came out "big," like oversized marbles. The report is saying the red blood cells are bigger than usual.

### Question 22

A- and an- mean "not," like saying "no thanks." Afebrile just means "no fever."

### Question 23

Dys- means something is "not working right," like a zipper that is stuck. Dyspnea means breathing is hard.

### Question 24

Anti- means "against," like a shield against rain. An antibiotic fights against germs.

### Question 25

Brady- means "slow," like a turtle walking. Bradycardia is a heart that beats too slowly.

### Question 26

Tachy- means "fast," like a race car. Tachycardia is a heart that beats too quickly.

### Question 27

Mal- means "bad," like a spoiled piece of fruit. A malignant growth is a "bad" one that can spread.

### Question 28

Contra- means "against," like voting against an idea. A contraindication is a reason NOT to use a medicine or treatment.

### Question 29

Neo- means "new," like a brand-new toy. A neoplasm is new tissue that grew where it should not have.

### Question 30

-algia means "ouch," like the pain of a stubbed toe. Neuralgia means nerve pain.

### Question 31

-osis means "something is not normal," like a sock with a hole in it. Arthrosis means a joint is not in its normal, healthy state.

### Question 32

-malacia means "getting soft," like ice cream melting. Osteomalacia means the bones are getting soft.

### Question 33

-sclerosis means "turned hard," like clay drying into a hard pot. Hardened arteries are stiff instead of stretchy.

### Question 34

-stenosis means "getting narrow," like a garden hose pinched so less water flows. A narrowed blood vessel or canal is a stenosis.

### Question 35

-plegia means the muscles "cannot move at all," like a car that will not start. It is complete paralysis.

### Question 36

-paresis means "weak," like an arm that is wobbly but can still move a little. It is less severe than full paralysis.

### Question 37

-penia means "too few," like a cookie jar that is almost empty. Leukopenia means there are too few white blood cells.

### Question 38

-rrhea means "flowing out," like water running from a faucet. Rhinorrhea is a runny nose.

### Question 39

-ptosis means "drooping," like a heavy backpack pulling your shoulders down. A drooping eyelid is an example of ptosis.

### Question 40

-centesis means "poke with a needle to take out fluid," like drawing juice from a fruit with a straw.

### Question 41

-graphy means "the act of writing it down," like taking a photo. It is the process, while the -gram is the picture you get.

### Question 42

-gram is the "picture" you end up with, like the photo after you press the button. An ECG is the photo of the heart's rhythm.

### Question 43

-pexy means "tie it in place," like tying a balloon string to a chair so it does not float away.

### Question 44

-tripsy means "to crush," like smashing ice into small pieces. Lithotripsy crushes a stone into tiny bits.

### Question 45

-lysis means "to break apart," like ice melting into water. Hemolysis is red blood cells breaking apart.

### Question 46

-desis means "to join together," like gluing two puzzle pieces so they stay put. Arthrodesis fuses a joint so it cannot move.

### Question 47

-logy means "the study of," like studying dinosaurs is "dinosaur-ology." Cardiology is studying the heart.

### Question 48

-logist means the "person who studies," like a scientist who studies stars is an astronomer. A cardiologist is the heart doctor.

### Question 49

-metry is the "measuring," while -meter is the "measuring tool." A thermometer is the tool; thermometry is using the tool to measure.

### Question 50

-otomy means "cut open," and -ectomy means "cut out." One makes a slice and stops; the other takes the whole thing out.

### Question 51

Gastritis is like the stomach getting red and sore inside. The word is just "stomach" plus "inflammation."

### Question 52

Nephrectomy is "kidney" plus "take it out." It means the surgeon removed a kidney.

### Question 53

Cardiology is the "study of the heart," just like biology is the study of living things.

### Question 54

Arthritis is a joint that is red, swollen, and sore. The word is "joint" plus "inflammation."

### Question 55

Hepatomegaly means the liver "grew too big." It is just "liver" plus "enlargement."

### Question 56

Osteoporosis means the bones become "holey," like a sponge, which makes them weak and easy to break.

### Question 57

Dermatitis means the skin is red and irritated, like a rash. It is "skin" plus "inflammation."

### Question 58

Hypoglycemia means the body's "sugar tank" is running low. Hypo- is the "low" clue at the start of the word.

### Question 59

Bradycardia is a heart beating "too slowly," like a drummer playing in slow motion.

### Question 60

Erythrocytopenia means "too few red blood cells," like having fewer red marbles in the jar than expected.

### Question 61

Pericarditis is the "wrapper" around the heart getting inflamed. Peri- tells you it is the outer covering, not the heart muscle itself.

### Question 62

Intracranial means "inside the head," like a ball inside a box. Intra- is the "inside" clue.

### Question 63

Polyneuropathy means "many nerves are sick at once," like many wires in a machine breaking together.

### Question 64

Endocarditis is the heart's "inside wallpaper" getting inflamed. Endo- points to the inside layer, not the muscle or outer sac.

### Question 65

Gastrostomy means "make a new doorway into the stomach." The three surgery words look alike, but each suffix tells a different story.
